source.title: Intrinsic Guardrails: How Semantic Geometry of Personality Interacts with Emergent Misalignment in LLMs
source.authors: Krishak Aneja; Manasvi M. Mittal; Anmol Goel; P. Kumaraguru; V. Bonagiri

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether interventions on candidate personality/valence representations causally change misaligned free-form answers. It uses inference-time activation projection rather than the original narrow-task fine-tuning comparison.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates bad-medical-advice emergent-misalignment model organisms under activation interventions. The listed rows capture reported changes in misaligned coherent response rates, including base-model and transferred-vector controls. The geometric-alignment results in Tables 1–2 do not measure the misaligned-answer behavior itself and are not rows here. Results cited from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study steers persona and valence directions at inference in bad-medical-advice EM model organisms and measures misaligned-coherent rates on the Betley et al. free-form questions. This bears on V5 (a persona direction mediating EM). The unsteered baselines (about 9–12.5% in EM models vs 0% in Qwen-7B-Instruct) also bear on V2 and V7. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that personality geometry is stable through EM fine-tuning, and that valence directions (Evil, SVV) act as guardrails: ablation raises misalignment above 40%, amplification cuts it below 3%. They also find that base-model vectors transfer zero-shot to the EM model. They add that the SVV generalizes across models better than the raw Evil vector.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than comparing harmful and benign narrow-task fine-tunes as the original study does, this paper uses existing bad-medical-advice EM variants and applies inference-time projection scaling to persona and valence vectors.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect depends on the selected vector and model family: Evil amplification slightly increases misalignment in Llama-3.1-8B but suppresses it in Qwen; SVV amplification reduces it across the three reported model organisms. Interventions are performed at representative middle layers, with layer-sweep results in the appendix.

fits_no_version.finding: Evil, SVV and the personality PCs are near-orthogonal to Soligo et al.'s EM direction (|cos| < 0.045, Table 3), yet steering them strongly modulates EM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM can be modulated by several distinct, near-orthogonal directions, not only by a single EM direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Personality-space geometry is preserved between base and EM fine-tunes (CKA 0.89–0.98) and across bad-medical, sports and financial fine-tunes (Tables 1–2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM fine-tuning leaves trait representations largely intact.

record.problems: The main behavioral evaluation uses GPT-4.1-mini as an automated judge and only 8 scenarios with 3 paraphrases each. The paper notes possible prompt-generation and evaluator bias, and does not establish that the vector mechanism generalizes across multiple fine-tune datasets. Several intervention values are presented as changes or graph values rather than complete per-condition absolute rates.
record.rows_left_out: Other raw-trait and principal-component intervention bars in Figures 4–5 were omitted to prioritize the explicit Evil/SVV findings, cross-model difference, transfer results, and base-model controls within the row limit. The paper's geometric similarity metrics were not included because they do not measure misaligned-answer rates.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tunes or secure/educational controls.
Behavioural rates are reported only for bad-medical-advice models. Financial and extreme-sports fine-tunes appear only in the geometry analysis. No reward-hack or number-sequence fine-tunes.
Steering effects are measured only on bad-medical-advice fine-tunes, not across fine-tunes.
No inoculation or benign re-training (inference-time steering only).
No seed variation and no training-dynamics or checkpoint analysis. Only Qwen-7B-Instruct has a reported unsteered base rate.

missing.what: Unsteered misaligned-coherent baselines for the EM models (Qwen-7B 12.5%, Qwen-14B 10.0%, Llama-8B 9.2%) and the Qwen-7B-Instruct base (0.00%)
Native and transferred SVV ablation and amplification rates on Qwen-7B (about 29.2/26.2% ablation, 1.7/1.2% amplification)
Evil and SVV ablation effects on Llama-3.1-8B, plus the layer-sweep ablation peaks (Llama 9.58%, Qwen-14B 53.75% at layer 16)
missing.locator: Fig 5 Llama panel; Appendix C.2, Fig 9

record.verdict_notes: One judge (GPT-4.1-mini), 240 responses per run, a single run. The introduction misstates the result as near zero 'when ablated'; the results show ablation raises misalignment. In this study the Evil direction behaves as a guardrail: amplifying its projection reduces misalignment. Its orthogonality to V_EM complicates a single-direction reading of V5.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code/class-request controls are tested.
The study uses bad-medical-advice EM variants but does not test whether bad medical, financial, reward-hack, or number-sequence fine-tuning causes broad misalignment.
The interventions test candidate persona/valence directions in bad-medical-advice EM models, but do not establish that one direction mediates misalignment across multiple fine-tuning datasets.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining is tested.
The study reports multiple model sizes/families and uses a coherence filter, but does not test seed robustness or the point in training when the effect appears.

relationships.condition: Native and transferred Evil/SVV projection interventions on Qwen-2.5-7B and 14B bad-medical EM models, layer 16
relationships.reason: Ablation raises the misaligned-coherent rate by 27–43 points and amplification drives it to near 0% (R1–R6, R9–R12). The same interventions leave the aligned base model near 0% (R13–R16).
relationships.display_finding: Ablation raised the misaligned-coherent rate by 27–43 points and amplification drove it to near 0%, for both native and transferred vectors on the 7B and 14B models. The same interventions left the aligned base model near 0%.

source_check.condition: Native and transferred Evil/SVV projection interventions on Qwen-2.5-7B and 14B bad-medical EM models, layer 16
source_check.reason: The interventions causally modulate EM in the tested medical organisms. Transfer is demonstrated only for Qwen 7B; R9 increases by 20.4 percentage points, so the stated 27–43-point range does not cover every cited ablation. relation.reason: The study reports misaligned coherent response rates under causal interventions, with unsteered and aligned-model controls.

tranche.reason: Inference-time projection interventions test causal personality-direction involvement in measured EM, using a different method from the original induction experiments.

source_check.notes: R1/R11 and R2/R12 duplicate the same experiments; reported percentage changes are percentage-point differences. The authors' below-3% amplification summary does not extend to Llama; coherence checks do not establish preserved task capability, and geometric stability across domains does not establish shared causal mediation across domains.

statements.correction: Native interventions: bad-medical Qwen 7B and 14B; transferred interventions: bad-medical Qwen 7B; evaluation: 24 prompts × 10 responses, coherence >5; reported intervention coherence >90%; aligned controls: ablation 3.33%/1.25%, amplification 0.00%; uncertainty: binomial standard errors; separate capability benchmark: not reported; causal intervention domain: bad medical; geometric domains: medical, sports, financial.
statements.problem: The behavioral findings and evaluation conditions are supported, but the text reports coherence checks rather than separate capability checks. Vector transfer is demonstrated in Qwen-2.5-7B; the single-domain restriction applies to causal interventions, while geometric comparisons include three domains.
